record.paper_title: Major open problems in chaos theory and nonlinear dynamics
record.context_brief: Arrow of time and velocity reversal
record.original_question: For the cosmological arrow of time, if the velocities of every object or every molecule in the universe were simultaneously reversed, would the universe still continue expanding? This asks whether macroscopic time asymmetry can persist under microscopic velocity reversal, and therefore whether chaos theory is relevant not only to the thermodynamic arrow of time but also to the cosmological arrow of time.

evidence.quote: Here we mention a few major open problems: 1. an effective description of chaos and turbulence, 2. rough dependence on initial data, 3. arrow of time

For the cosmological arrow of time, one may ask the question: Is the universe still expanding if the velocity of every object (or every molecule) is simultaneously reversed? If the answer is yes, then chaos theory may still be relevant.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the universe modeled as a large collection of interacting particles (objects/molecules) whose dynamics are governed by time-reversible microscopic laws, and which on macroscopic scales is observed to be expanding (a cosmological arrow of time). Suppose that at some instant the velocity of every particle in the universe is simultaneously reversed (i.e., the state (x_i, v_i) is replaced by (x_i, -v_i) for every particle i), while all positions are kept fixed. Determine whether, under the resulting dynamics, the universe would continue to expand, or whether instead the macroscopic expansion would reverse into a contraction. Equivalently: does the cosmological arrow of time (expansion versus contraction of the universe) persist under simultaneous reversal of all microscopic velocities, in the way that chaotic/mixing dynamics is believed to make the thermodynamic arrow of time persist under such reversal?
artifact.category_tag: Arrow of time and cosmological dynamics
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the cosmological arrow of time would persist under simultaneous reversal of all microscopic velocities is a recognized foundational open problem connecting chaos theory, statistical mechanics, and cosmology; no rigorous answer is established in the literature.
